_comment: Copy to permissions.json (gitignored) and edit. install.sh merges the 'allow' list into the permissions.allow of ~/.claude/settings.json. Rules use Claude Code's permission syntax. Absolute paths are machine-specific; keep them out of version control. If permissions.json is absent, install.sh skips the merge and leaves existing permissions untouched.
_comment_harness: Why the harness lines above. A node session drives the tree entirely through that CLI and invokes it by path, so none of the other rules match it and every call falls through to the auto-mode classifier. That classifier keys on command text, which makes it non-deterministic here: a read-only `harness queue dev` was allowed twice and blocked on the third identical call, and a `harness grant` was blocked until the same flags were re-sent with shorter prose. A lead that cannot reliably run `grant` cannot approve anything, and one that cannot run `recycle` cannot replace a member. A Bash rule matches the command TEXT, not the resolved path, so every spelling a session might type needs its own line — bare name, tilde, and absolute.
